newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 19.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* President Clinton urged negotiators in tobacco-settlement talks to keep pursuing an agreement, but would not preclude getting involved personally if he believes hopes of reaching a deal have been exhausted.
* Unisys Corp Chairman and Chief Executive James Unruh is expected to announce plans to step down.
* A Federal Reserve survey known as the beige book shows "pockets of weakness" in the 12 districts it monitors.
* Westinghouse has changed its plans to separate its media and industrial businesses and has decided that the Thermo King refrigerated transport group will remain part of its media division.
* Loews Corp has acquired 50,000 shares of Delta Air Lines Inc for $4.2 million in the first quarter.
* Large computer resellers to businesses said there was a drop in demand for personal computers in the first quarter and into April that has reversed itself.
* Technology stocks took a hit after Seagate Technology Inc and Gateway 2000 Inc offered grim earnings forecasts.
* Goldman Sachs & Co posted a record $1.52 billion in earnings in the first half of its fiscal year, a 19 percent increase from the same period in the prior year.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission has dropped its last remaining investigation into former employees of Prudential Securities and their possible roles in sales of limited partnerships.
* British Aerospace Plc has joined Lockheed Martin in its bid for the multibillion-dollar U.S. joint strike fighter program.
* Viacom Inc is asking movie studio to reduce the prices of videos they sell to its Blockbuster unit by as much as 15 percent.
* Herbert Denton, a shareholder activist, said that Digital Equipment Corp will likely be pushed to name new, younger directors.
* Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt is expected to criticize a possible merger between AT&T Corp with regional Bell SBC Communications.
